what: A change to running code — an edit at a seam in the implementation. Yields code; proved by exercising that code.
why: The default, most common node kind: work that compiles to a behavioral change. Distinct from skill (proved by cairnmap recompile) and concept-piece (proved by human review) — a code-seam is proved by the tester running a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. Named 'seam' not 'code' because the unit is the behavior/interface boundary the change lands at, where a proof can grip.

v1.why: The machine-readable transition table the emit-chokepoint (cairn/base/transitions.py) validates a node's workflow string against — turning /sorted's prose 'refuses illegal transitions' into physics (Law 4, state-machine-physics.json). `path` is the versioned canonical sequence a code-seam@v1 string must conform to; a drifted path is refused. `skippable_summons` names the ONE fork the -ME grammar cannot derive: TICKETME is optional (a leaf goes THINKME->BUILDME, a parent goes THINKME->TICKETME; 'waiting on children' is derived, not a stored state). Forward advances or skips only skippable summonses; back-edges re-enter any earlier summons (kick-back). Rests (no -ME: PROVED) and summonses (-ME) are grammar-derived, not stored here. FILED: the LEARNING driver-terminal (a code ticket becomes a driver by editing its tail -> LEARNING) is a workflow migration, a later version; concept-piece/host-seam get their own tables (state-machine-physics children, pending). AMENDED 2026-07-30 (ticket watchme-emits-a-probe): the FILED driver-terminal above is VACANT — LEARNING is dissolved as a node state, so 'editing its tail -> LEARNING' names a state that no longer exists. What a code-seam would be edited TO in order to become an operational-driver is now an open ruling awaiting Akien's signature gate; see node_classes/operational-driver.json `open_ruling`. The clause is amended rather than struck because v1 is a REGISTERED version and its record must keep the shape it had (Law 7); nothing is at sea, because that migration was never built.

v2.why:
Minted 2026-07-30 (ticket watchme-emits-a-probe). THE FIFTH SUMMONS LEAVES THE PATH ENTIRELY (v1 carries it; it is dissolved, and tickets/watchme-emits-a-probe is its one record) and WATCHME is not its replacement in the same seat — the shape changes, which is why this is a NEW VERSION and not a widening of v1 (versions are immutable and version-stamped; migration-by-find-and-replace is the mechanism MAP.md already names). WHAT WAS WRONG WITH v1: that summons sat in `path` with only TICKETME skippable, so it was MANDATORY TO CROSS for every node of this class and carried NO GATE — the one summons in the path that was forced and unchecked. Akien's rule is the exact inverse: OPTIONAL TO CARRY, MANDATORY TO SATISFY ONCE CARRIED. Under forced-and-unchecked the crossing got filled with whatever was at hand (on ticket a-node-holds-one-claim, 2026-07-29, it was close-bookkeeping — not efficacy data at all, and the node never dwelled).

HOW THE INVERSION IS SPELLED: WATCHME is a FREE SUMMONS — it may appear ZERO OR MORE TIMES AT ANY POSITION, so it is absent from `path` (the backbone) and declared in `free_summons` instead. Optional to carry = the ticket author puts it in the string or does not. Mandatory to satisfy = once it IS in the string it is NOT in `skippable_summons`, so the chokepoint's forward walk cannot step over it. The two declarations are orthogonal on purpose: `skippable_summons` is the FORK a node takes at runtime, `free_summons` is the SHAPE the ticket authored.

AND IT MUST NAME ITS OBJECT. `WATCHME(what-it-watches)` — a bare WATCHME is refused by _conform, because a watch without an object is inert (Akien 2026-07-30): a bare token cannot state what is being watched, so nothing can check it. Forced by structure the way intention+why.json forces the why, never a blank field someone can leave empty.

THE REST IS UNCHANGED FROM v1 and deliberately so: the backbone, TICKETME as the one skippable fork, the build gate at the PROVEME crossing, the entry gate into BUILDME and the exit gate into PROVED all keep their seats. A ticket with a WATCHME crosses PROVEME forward INTO its watch (build gate fires there, as before — the gate is on crossing OF the PROVEME summons) and then into PROVED (exit gate fires there, as before). A ticket with no WATCHME reads exactly like v1 with the dissolved summons removed.

WHY THE TICKET CREATES A PROBE RATHER THAN BECOMING ONE (Akien's ruling 2026-08-03, which corrected two words at once: EMISSION WAS THE WRONG WORD, and it is a TICKET that crosses a gate — 'node' is ambiguous, the system has several kinds). A proved intention's efficacy data can only accumulate AFTER it rests, so a ticket that WAITS for it never rests and never gets measured. WATCHME's act is to CREATE A PROBE (cairn/base/probe.py — immutable; trigger/carrier/enough all open predicates): the probe is attached to the ticket and aimed wherever the feedback has to come from — a gateway, a time, a future event, whatever — and it carries who to call back, which is whoever attached it or another target designated at creation. ONCE THAT PROBE IS CREATED, THE STATE IS COMPLETE. The ticket rests at PROVED; the probe stands, and fires when its crossing comes. That deletes a state rather than adding one.

prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the node's proof and emits a VALIDATION; verdict and seal from the same hand. IOU: the tester isn't built, so proof is hand-run per the node's proofs/PROOF.md, culminating in a measured VALIDATION recorded by hand.
extra_gates: durability gate — a code-seam is not done until tested AND durably committed (git). Durability-of-stones sits on the emit chokepoint (physics, MAP.md 'Gates, not supervisors'), not a step anyone remembers to run: commit often (commit notes are notes to future selves), push at 'smells like done'. (Akien refinement 2026-07-15 — traces to the founding intention of getting Akien out of running the system.)
kicks_back_on: red proof (behavior doesn't match the falsifier) → routes back to design/build at the point of creation (CP2).
provenance: first code-seam, defined 2026-07-15 when the first running-code change was cast — discovered as demanded, not pre-seeded (the slate predicted this). Ratified by Akien (signature gate) 2026-07-15.
